reason: Bahdanau additive attention: scores = Linear_A(tanh(U f + W h)), softmax, then an einsum-weighted sum. The scores come from a tanh MLP, not QK^T, and the rubric lists additive MLP-score attention as a keep.

The score is a linear layer on concat(curr_node, x_j). The curr_node term is constant over j, so it cancels in the softmax, leaving softmax_j(x_j . w_b) followed by a weighted sum of x_j. That is single-query (decode-style) dot-product attention pooling with a learned query and K=V=x. It reads as additive scoring (a keep), but its math and kernel are single-query SDPA, so I can't place it cleanly.

MLP-score (Bahdanau) attention: tanh(ctx Wc + hid Wh) w_mlp / temp, softmax over axis 0, weighted sum of ctx, then a projection. The scores come from an additive tanh MLP, not QK^T, which the rubric marks as a keep.

Sigmoid on the logits, gather of the label probability, then a dice-style 1 - (p(1-p)+eps)/(p(1-p)+1+eps) and a mean. There is no softmax or log-sum-exp over classes, so the math differs from CE (dice losses are a listed keep).

About 99.6% of FLOPs are a GEMM + bias + LeakyReLU (512->512), which is the 20k chain minus its x2 scale. The only addition is a 512->2 projection epilogue that contracts the hidden dimension to a tiny output, the same kernel shape as the 36k Matmul->act->Sum reduction.

Linear projections plus biaffine scoring: a bilinear s^T U_n t_n per teacher, plus linear terms, then a softmax over teachers. There is no QK^T-then-V aggregation, and the three-operand bilinear contraction fused with the projections is not a JAXBench algorithm.

gMLP spatial gating unit: a LayerNorm (centred) over features on half the channels, a sequence-axis token-mixing GEMM with bias, then gating by the other half. The GEMM is wrapped in a non-trivial LayerNorm prologue and a tensor-gate epilogue, so it is more than a plain linear with a bias.

ArcFace loss: L2-normalize over channels, a GEMM, an arccos/cos angular margin on the target, and a sum of exp(s*cos) over non-target channels. The log-sum-exp runs over a batch axis of the GEMM (C), not its output/vocab dimension, so it is neither plain CE nor fused linear-CE.
Purely elementwise: a PACT clip to [0, |alpha|], then k-bit uniform rounding. No JAXBench task has this algorithm.

Plain non-causal single-head cross-attention: Q from a 1x1 conv over HW=4096 pixels, K/V from linear projections of 256 centers, softmax(QK^T)V, then scale*out + x. The attention matmuls dominate FLOPs, and the projections and residual are the trivial wrapping the rubric says to exclude.

Pairwise squared differences, a per-dimension median bandwidth via sort, a bandwidth-weighted sum, and an IMQ power. This is a pairwise-distance kernel with a median reduction, unlike any JAXBench task.

Concat/additive attention: tanh(W[h; enc]) . v gives the scores, then softmax, a multiplicative mask, renormalization, and a bmm context. The scores come from an additive tanh MLP (Bahdanau-style), not QK^T, which the rubric marks as a keep.

torch Bilinear (x1^T W_k x2 for 128 outputs) plus a linear on concat(x1, x2). There is no softmax. The dominant work is a GEMM whose epilogue contracts with the per-row second operand (a bilinear form), which is not a plain GEMM or any JAXBench task.

Sinkhorn-sort-net routing: cumulative averages, bucket summaries, a small QK^T between buckets with a causal-style mask, then a softmax and a differentiable top-1 (max/argmax/one-hot). There is no V aggregation, and the cumavg scan plus top-k selection make it different from softmax(QK^T)V.
Elementwise BCE-with-logits (sigmoid, not a softmax over classes) plus a per-channel soft Dice reduction. It shares no algorithm with softmax CE, and dice losses are a listed keep.

A 3-layer ReLU MLP with a log_softmax over 10 classes. The first layer (~86% of FLOPs) is exactly the 41k Gemm+bias+ReLU chain, but the second 512->128 layer (~14%) and the narrow head make it a fused multi-GEMM pipeline rather than one k-task. Every component is a JAXBench op, so I can't call it materially different.

ASTGCN spatial attention: two reductions of the large x tensor (over T and over F), which dominate bytes, then a bmm, +bias, sigmoid, a learned NxN Vs matmul and a column softmax. It outputs the attention map with no V aggregation, and the multi-stage chain with sigmoid in the middle is neither SDPA nor a k-task chain.

Concurrent spatial and channel squeeze-excitation: a sigmoid gate from a 1x1 conv over channels plus a sigmoid gate from avgpool->MLP. These are SE-style sigmoid gates, which the rubric marks as a keep.

A 3-layer MLP with ELU and a centred LayerNorm after each hidden layer, then a sigmoid. FLOPs are spread across three GEMMs and two LayerNorm row reductions sit between them, so it is a multi-part network, not a single JAXBench GEMM chain.

A GEGLU gate: x @ [W_val | W_gate] + b, split, val * gelu(gate). This is the fused dual-GEMM with gated-activation epilogue that forms the core of 9p (GeGLU is listed under 9p). The only differences are GELU vs SiLU, the biases, and the missing down projection.

torch broadcasting turns the score into 512 batched 512x512x512 matrix products (values[y,z] @ query[x,y]). The softmax then runs elementwise over a size-8 broadcast axis y, and the context is an elementwise weighted sum. That is not a row softmax of QK^T followed by a V matmul, so the algorithm differs from SDPA.

Two GEMMs share the input x and their outputs are multiplied, as in the gate/up half of 9p: relu(xWn+b) * softmax(xWg+b, axis=0), plus a (1-gate)*x highway. Unlike 9p there is no down projection, and the gate is a softmax over the leading batch axis, which needs all 16 batch slices in one block. It is unclear whether that makes it a different algorithm.

The core is a grouped conv2d cross-correlation (16 groups of 256 channels, a 16x16 kernel over a 128x128 search image) followed by a scale. A grouped large-kernel conv is not 18k's dense 3x3 Conv+ReLU+bias chain, and the rubric keeps convolutions.

A GRU cell: z and r GEMMs with sigmoid on [h,x], then a third GEMM on [r*h, x] with tanh, then (1-z)h + z*t. The reset gate acts on the hidden state before a dependent third GEMM, and the output is a z-weighted interpolation. That is materially different math from up*act(gate)@down, though the overall shape resembles 9p.

Co-attention: one score matrix x1 x2^T feeds two masked softmaxes (over each axis), each multiplied back onto x2 or x1. Each direction is softmax(QK^T + padding mask)V with V=K, which the rubric counts as SDPA with a mask; sharing the score matrix does not change that.

Two non-causal 4-head cross-attentions softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V over 2048x2048 tokens are the largest part (~45% of FLOPs) and dominate bytes. The rest is Linear+bias+ReLU projections, which is exactly 41k's chain, so every substantial part is a JAXBench algorithm.

There is no Sinkhorn normalisation. It applies a tiny pointwise MLP to scalars: a K=1 outer product + ReLU, then a 32x32 linear, expanding 16.7M scalars into ~1 GB of output. It is memory-bound broadcast expansion, not a GEMM-bound design like 8p/41k, and has nothing in common with 56p.

Three equal-sized 512x512 Linear layers (ELU, sigmoid, none). Each layer is the 8p/41k GEMM+bias+activation algorithm differing only in the activation. The only new element is chaining three layers (fusable into one MLP kernel), and the rubric does not settle whether that makes it a new algorithm.

The dominant layer (784->500, ~75% of FLOPs) is exactly 41k's Gemm+bias+ReLU. The second layer is 41k again and the head (Linear + softmax over features) is exactly 38k's Matmul+softmax, so the whole problem is built from JAXBench k-task chains.

A full transformer block: LayerNorm, two MHSA sublayers (SDPA with an additive task embedding on q/k), and a LayerNorm + GELU FFN, each with a residual. SDPA is only ~20% of FLOPs, with QKV/out projections, the FFN and three LayerNorms making up the rest. This is the rubric's 'attention is one part among several substantial parts' keep case.

A two-GEMM FFN (1024->4096 ReLU ->1024) with a residual + LayerNorm epilogue. It has 9p's fused up->act->down structure but no gate projection, and the LayerNorm epilogue needs a full-row reduction after the down GEMM. It is neither clearly 9p nor clearly new.
Single-head non-causal SDPA (4096 tokens, head dim 256, unscaled) between 1x1-conv Q/K/V/output projections. The attention is ~90% of FLOPs, so the core is softmax(QK^T)V.

Elementwise sigmoid binary cross-entropy (log_sigmoid terms) times a mask, summed over the last axis, then a mean. There is no softmax/logsumexp over classes and no integer targets, so the math differs from 13p's softmax CE.

Soft-assignment pooling (NetVLAD/Encoding layer): softmax over 32 codewords of per-code scaled squared L2 distances, then aggregation A^T X - (sum A) c. The aggregation contracts over the token (query) axis, not the key axis, so it is a different contraction from softmax(QK^T)V. It is also memory-bound with only 32 codes.
Softmax over channels, then global sums of p*t and p+t and 1 - ratio. The rubric names Dice loss as a keep: different math from softmax cross-entropy.

Two branches on a shared input, each Linear+bias -> softmax -> ReLU (the ReLU is a no-op after softmax). That is 38k's Matmul+bias+softmax chain, but the softmax runs over dim1 (a strided group of 64 rows) instead of the feature axis, which changes the epilogue's reduction axis.

DANet channel attention is Gram-matrix attention, not an SE gate: softmax(rowmax - F F^T) F. Softmax is shift-invariant, so this is softmax(-QK^T)V with Q=K=V=F (512 channels as tokens, head dim HW=4096). That is SDPA with an elementwise score mod (negation), differing from 1p only in shape.

VQA MLP-score attention: relu(vWv+b) * relu(qWq+b), then Linear, then softmax over objects. This is not SDPA, and the rubric keeps MLP-score attention. But ~94% of FLOPs is a single Gemm+bias+ReLU identical to 41k plus a broadcast multiply, so the two rubric signals conflict.

Attention U-Net additive gate: conv1x1(x) + conv1x1(g), ReLU, a 1x1 conv to one channel, then sigmoid. This is an additive/sigmoid attention gate (a rubric keep), and with K=128 the fused kernel is memory-bound; it is neither SDPA nor a k-task chain.

FLOPs are a plain GEMM+bias (2048->128), i.e. 8p, but bytes and time are dominated by a 128x broadcast-add expansion into a (N,128,128) output of ~268 MB. The kernel design is mostly a memory-bound broadcast write rather than GEMM tiling, so it is unclear whether the core counts as 8p.
BoTNet MHSA: softmax(q_i.k_j + rel_i.q_j)V, i.e. SDPA plus an additive learned relative-position content-position term (Transformer-XL-style). The rubric names this explicitly as exclude, closest 5p.
4-head non-causal SDPA (2048x2048, unscaled, projected key reused as value) is ~67% of FLOPs. Q/K projections and a concat + Linear + tanh output are minor. The core is softmax(QK^T)V.

The core is an elementwise multiply, a sum over 64 channels and a softmax over the batch axis (size 8). It is a memory-bound reduction with no QK^T matmul and no V aggregation, so it is not attention in the softmax(QK^T)V sense and matches no JAXBench algorithm.

This is a full transformer block: three LayerNorm plus cross-attention branches with their Q/K/V/out projections, a concat, then LayerNorm and a GELU MLP (1536->2048->1536). The SDPA core is about 25% of FLOPs (~103G of ~412G); projections are ~103G and the MLP ~206G. That makes attention one substantial part among several, which the rubric keeps.

With C=128 the active path is argmax(target, axis=1), a gather of log(output) at that index, and a mean. There is no logits matmul and no softmax/logsumexp normalisation. Those are what define 13p's fused linear + CE kernel; this is a memory-bound argmax-plus-gather.

The core is an elementwise weighted binary cross-entropy with logits (log_sigmoid terms), summed over the last axis and averaged. It is a pointwise op plus a reduction, with no softmax over classes, so it is different math from softmax CE.

The core is elementwise BCE on probabilities plus per-sample Dice reductions (intersection and sums). Binary CE and Dice are both listed by the rubric as different math from softmax CE, and there is no matmul.

The learned 1x1 conv only projects the context into a shared K=V (0.27 GFLOP). The core (~8.6 GFLOP) is softmax(target^T @ source) @ source: unscaled, single-head, non-causal cross-attention over 4096 queries and 128 keys, i.e. SDPA. Returning the attention matrix is only an extra output.

This is additive (Bahdanau-style) attention pooling: tanh(x@W1)@w2 gives a scalar score per position, softmax runs over the sequence, and the output is a weighted sum of x. There is no QK^T score matrix, and the rubric explicitly keeps additive MLP-score attention.

The work is two Linear+bias+ReLU layers. The first (4096x12544 @ 12544x1024) is ~92% of FLOPs and is exactly 41k's Gemm -> Add(bias) -> ReLU chain; the second layer is the same chain at a smaller size. The 'glu_mlp' flag is wrong because there is no gating.
These are three stacked Linear+bias+ReLU layers, and the first (16384x3072 @ 3072x512) is ~85% of FLOPs. Every layer is exactly 41k's Gemm -> bias add -> ReLU chain, with only the shapes changed.

This is ASTGCN temporal attention: two vector contractions of a large (B,N,F,T) tensor (memory-bound), a (T,N)@(N,T) product, a sigmoid with a bias, a Ve @ (T,T) matmul, and a softmax over dim 1 as the output. There is no softmax-weighted aggregation of V and the score path goes through a sigmoid and a second matmul, so it is not softmax(QK^T)V.

This is standard non-causal multi-head attention (8 heads, d=128, L=2048): per-head shared Q/K/V linears, softmax(QK^T/sqrt(E)), AV, then an output projection. The SDPA core is ~75% of FLOPs, and the different scale constant is only a constant change.

These are three equal-sized 512x512 Linear layers over 131072 rows: two Linear+bias+ReLU (exactly 41k's chain) and a final Linear+bias (8p). Every layer is a plain GEMM with a bias and at most a ReLU, so the core is the 41k/8p algorithm.

The core is a sigmoid followed by per-sample Dice reductions (intersection and union sums). Dice loss is listed by the rubric as different math from CE, and it is an elementwise plus reduction kernel with no JAXBench counterpart.

This is CBAM spatial attention: channel max and mean pooling, a 2->1 3x3 conv, a sigmoid, and an elementwise gate on x. It is a sigmoid gating module, not softmax(QK^T)V, and the rubric explicitly keeps it.

The core is softmax cross-entropy over the 128-class axis (log_softmax plus a gather at an integer label), summed. The label is a masked argmax that folds into the same per-pixel reduction pass over classes, so it is plain softmax CE with integer targets, which the rubric maps to 13p.
The core is global sums of p*t and p^2+t^2 combined into a Dice ratio. It is a pure elementwise plus full reduction kernel, and the rubric keeps Dice loss as different math.

This is additive attention pooling: Linear->tanh->Linear produces feature-wise scores, softmax runs over axis 1, then a weighted sum over that axis. FLOPs are dominated by the two 512x512 GEMMs and there is no QK^T score matrix, so it is the additive/MLP-score attention the rubric keeps.

This is standard non-causal MHA (4 heads, hd=128, N=2048): a 1x1-conv QKV projection, softmax(QK^T/sqrt(hd))V, and a 1x1-conv output projection. The SDPA core (~137 GFLOP) dominates the projections (~69 GFLOP).

The core is single-head, non-causal, unscaled softmax(QK^T)V over 4096 spatial positions with d=512 (~275 GFLOP), while the 1x1-conv Q/K/V projections are ~52 GFLOP. The gamma*out + x residual is trivial post-processing, so this is the SDPA algorithm.

The core is uncentred norm-and-scale: x / (sqrt(sum_c x^2) + eps) * weight[c], a single memory-bound reduction followed by normalise and scale. That is RMSNorm's algorithm. Sum instead of mean only rescales the result by the constant sqrt(C), eps sits after the sqrt rather than inside, and the reduction runs over the NCHW channel axis instead of the last axis, which is a layout difference. None of these changes the kernel design.

Same computation as L2Norm_13237 in f32 with a smaller width: per-pixel channel L2 normalisation x / (sqrt(sum_c x^2) + eps) times a per-channel weight. This is RMSNorm (x * rsqrt(mean(x^2)+eps) * w) up to a constant factor, eps placement and the reduction axis, so it is the same reduce-normalise-scale algorithm as 12p.
